strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Building pricing governance and deal pricing for a publicly funded lab network that is growing private B2B and B2C revenue
strategy_updates.current_model: Most individual diagnostic tests are covered by provincial plans (OHIP, BC MSP, Saskatchewan); uncovered tests are self-pay with fees disclosed at the visit. Published consumer prices include LifeLabs Comes to You mobile collection at $85 per person and pre-departure COVID-19 testing at $80; at-home kits are sold separately. Government and corporate contracts are not priced publicly.
posting_evidence: Senior Manager, Pricing in Toronto, published about three weeks before Oct 19, 2026 on Jobillico (internal ref. 20850); CAD 112,565-143,520.
Reports to the Director, Financial Planning & Analysis Revenues & Operations; advises senior leaders including the CFO and CEO.
Mandate covers pricing strategy, frameworks and policies across Government, B2B and B2C lines, plus deal, RFP and new-product pricing with the commercial teams.
Owns price-volume-mix, price realization, discount leakage and contract-profitability analytics; builds pricing assumptions into the annual and long-range plans.
Establishes pricing governance (approval thresholds, decision rights, escalation) and automates RFP and contract workflows, including AI-enabled tools; Oracle/EPM and Power BI.
strategy_updates.interpretation: LifeLabs' core revenue comes from provincial fee arrangements it cannot price freely, so the role's leverage is in the parts it can price: government and B2B contracts, RFPs, and direct-to-consumer services. The emphasis on discount leakage, approval thresholds and decision rights suggests deal pricing is currently decided case by case and the company wants central control (inference). Putting the role in FP&A, with margin and plan integration, points to protecting margin rather than growth-led pricing. As part of Quest Diagnostics since 2024, it may also be aligning with parent-company pricing discipline (unconfirmed).
open_questions: Which revenue lines are open to pricing decisions, and how big are B2B and B2C relative to provincial funding?
Will the role own approval rights on deals or only advise Commercial?
How much do Quest's pricing practices and tools shape the remit?
strategy_updates.caveat: Analysis is based on a Jobillico copy of the posting and LifeLabs' patient pricing page; no pricing news from the last three months was found, and the official Dayforce page could not be read.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Adding junior actuarial capacity to model rates and run profitability and rate-adjustment analyses
posting_evidence: Actuario junior de pricing, Bogotá, published Sep 23, 2026 on elempleo; hybrid, full-time, indefinite contract; salary confidential.
Builds pricing models under supervision and takes part in profitability, sensitivity and rate-adjustment analyses.
Automates actuarial reports and processes with R, Python and SQL; prepares and cleans modelling data; documents models and assumptions.
Requires an actuarial, mathematics, statistics or engineering degree, 1-2 years of experience (the listing is inconsistent), Power BI and experience developing and validating pricing models.
strategy_updates.interpretation: This is a capacity hire inside an existing actuarial pricing team, not a strategy role: the work is model building, automation and rate-sensitivity analysis under supervision. The focus on automating reports suggests the team wants faster rate reviews (inference). The posting does not name the product line, so it may be motor, home or life pricing; no recent pricing news was found to show which.
open_questions: Which lines of business (auto, home, ARL, life) does the team price?
What is the path from junior actuary to pricing lead, and how are rate changes approved?
strategy_updates.caveat: Single junior posting from a job board, with no product line named and no pricing news found; the interpretation is thin.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Building a monetization and price-realization bench across self-serve, enterprise and platform-level packaging on a usage-priced platform
strategy_updates.current_model: Pay-as-you-go usage pricing per message and minute (SMS from $0.0083, outbound voice $0.014 per minute) with volume discounts as usage grows; Video billed per participant minute from $0.004 (pricing page dated August 2026); custom enterprise deals through sales; some per-user pricing (Flex at $150 per named user per month). Carrier A2P fees are passed through at cost.
posting_evidence: New US-remote Principal Pricing and Monetization Manager (Greenhouse 8284815, marked New; applications intended to close Nov 19): pricing and packaging strategy for incremental revenue and margin, aligning product roadmaps to monetization frameworks; reports to the Director of Monetization & Pricing Strategy.
It asks for 8+ years in pricing including 5+ owning pricing and monetization in telecom/SaaS/PaaS, multi-product platform pricing, and conjoint/Van Westendorp research.

Two US-remote Principal Price Realization Strategy Managers (Digital & PLG; Enterprise & Account-Led), first published Jun 16, 2026, still live on Oct 19; both report to the Director of Price Realization Strategy.
All three share the same pay bands ($141,520-$208,000 by location) and exclude hiring in CA, CT, NJ, NY, PA and WA.
The earlier Colombia-based Senior Price Realization Strategy Manager (JOB-0033) is no longer on the board.

news.summary: Q2 2026: revenue $1.50B (+22% reported, 17% organic); dollar-based net expansion 116% vs 108% a year earlier; non-GAAP gross margin 49% vs 51%; full-year reported growth guidance raised to 18-18.5%; release cites 'price actions' among margin factors and notes carrier fees are passed through at cost.

strategy_updates.interpretation: Twilio now has two teams side by side: price realization (discount and list-price capture across PLG and enterprise) and monetization and pricing strategy (packaging and frameworks for the multi-product platform). The new principal role focuses on revenue and margin from packaging, which fits a company whose net expansion is rising while gross margin falls (inference). Adding it in October, after the realization roles, suggests the next step is platform-level bundles or packaging across products rather than per-API price points (inference). The role is senior individual-contributor work with heavy cross-functional influence and no team.
open_questions: Which products or bundles does the new monetization role own, and how does it split work with the price realization team?
Is Twilio moving toward platform or bundle pricing, for example for AI voice and Conversation Intelligence?
How much of the gross margin decline comes from pricing versus mix and carrier fees?
strategy_updates.caveat: The postings name no products; the link to margin pressure is inference from earnings. Third-party trackers reported Video repricing, but Twilio's own Video page still shows per-minute pricing, so that was not used.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Monetizing AI across a newly re-tiered portfolio: pricing-committee governance, deal guardrails and operationalizing new commercial models
strategy_updates.current_model: No public list prices. Since April 9, 2026, products are sold in Foundation, Advanced and Prime tiers that bundle AI layers previously sold separately (AI Control Tower, Workflow Data Fabric, a Context Engine). Licensing is per seat plus other meters such as assets and storage, with a pool of AI usage included per product and extra usage billed (per trade press).
posting_evidence: As of Oct 19, 2026, ServiceNow's SmartRecruiters search for 'pricing' shows a Monetization Strategy Manager (744000150761409, San Diego, 'Flexible or Remote', $114,200-$199,900 base), a Monetization Strategy Director (744000146501509) and a Pricing Operations Senior Analyst in Costa Rica.
The other Monetization Strategy Manager (JB0075274, JOB-0038) and the Senior Director, Pricing Operations Transformation (JOB-0040) are closed.

Manager: supports C-suite-sponsored top-line initiatives; bridges Product Pricing and Deal Desk to set commercial principles and guardrails; 5+ years in enterprise tech pricing, consulting or strategy; asks for experience applying AI to the work.
Director: monetization lead for CRM and Industry Workflows; Pricing Committee preparation, BU 3-year plans, conjoint and other pricing research.

news.summary: Q2 2026: subscription revenue $3,877M (+24.5%), cRPO $13.20B (+21%); ServiceNow AI crossed $1B in annual contract value; full-year subscription guidance raised to $15,760-15,780M and Q3 subscription guidance set at $3,975-3,980M.

strategy_updates.interpretation: With one manager role and the operations senior director closed, ServiceNow has kept one manager seat between product pricing and deal desk and the CRM director role open, so governance of AI-tier deals is still the hiring priority (inference). A pricing operations analyst in Costa Rica suggests execution work is moving to a lower-cost hub while strategy stays in the US (inference). The open questions remain how AI value is captured through tier upgrades versus usage above included pools, and how strictly discounting is controlled.
open_questions: How are included AI usage pools sized per tier, and how is overage priced?
Which business units does the remaining manager role cover?
Will Q3 results (due late October) report AI-tier upgrade or usage metrics?
strategy_updates.caveat: Tier details come from trade press; ServiceNow publishes no prices and the postings name few products.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Raising AI compute prices into tight GPU supply while building a central pricing and discount-governance function
strategy_updates.current_model: On-demand GPU instances priced per GPU-hour in USD (H100 $4.50, H200 $5.40, B200 $8.50, B300 $9.50; RTX PRO 6000 $1.80; L40S from $1.55); GB200/GB300 NVL72 on request; lower rates for multi-month reserved clusters through sales; market-driven spot prices; Token Factory inference priced separately. Prices exclude VAT and Nebius may change them at any time.
posting_evidence: Director, Pricing (Finance), remote with a San Francisco Bay Area office listed; first published Jun 26, 2026, updated Oct 13; no salary stated.
Owns company-wide pricing for GPU infrastructure, cloud products, Token Factory and future offerings: list prices, tiers, commitment structures and regional approaches.
Turns unit economics and margin targets into price floors and margin ranges; evaluates profitability by SKU, region and customer segment.
Owns the discount framework (matrices, approval thresholds, guardrails, escalation), monitors realized pricing and leakage, and runs regular pricing reviews; pricing must follow SOX procedures.
Works with Unit Economics, Market Intelligence and Packaging, Deal Desk, Finance, Product and Sales; 7-12 years in pricing, monetization or commercial finance.

news.summary: Nebius told customers it would raise on-demand GPU prices from Oct 1, 2026: H100 $3.85 to $4.50, H200 $4.50 to $5.40, B200 $7.15 to $8.50, B300 $7.85 to $9.50 per GPU-hour (up to about 21%), with preemptible moving to dynamic spot pricing.
news.source: KuCoin News (citing Odaily and a Nebius customer notice)

news.summary: UsagePricing recorded the same Oct 1 GPU-hour increases on Nebius's price list, with RTX PRO 6000 and L40S unchanged; Nebius's own price page now shows the new on-demand rates.

strategy_updates.interpretation: Nebius is using strong demand to raise list prices and push customers toward commitments and dynamic spot pricing. That makes discount discipline and price floors worth more than list-price design. The posting's focus on price floors, margin ranges, discount matrices and leakage, plus SOX alignment, points to a scaling public company that wants pricing centrally governed under Finance rather than set deal by deal (inference). The director would likely own how commitment discounts and regional prices hold up against the higher list prices.
open_questions: How much revenue is on-demand versus reserved commitments, and how are commitment discounts set today?
Does the role cover Token Factory per-token pricing as well as GPU-hour pricing?
Which countries can the 'Remote' role be hired in?
strategy_updates.caveat: News on the price increase comes from secondary outlets citing a customer notice, though Nebius's price page confirms the new on-demand rates. Commitment and Token Factory pricing were not reviewed.
